as_told.title: Nimitz tic-tac case and its infrared footage

plain: In 2004, off Southern California, a heat-sensing camera on a Navy jet filmed a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint. The camera is called forward-looking infrared, or FLIR. Michels calls it "the famous tic tac video", and he says the thermal image is the best picture of the whole case, which is tied to the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz. A guest named Merrick von Renenamp, retelling what the crews reported, explains how the video came about. After the first jets returned to the carrier, the Navy pilot David Fravor reportedly told another pilot, Chad Underwood, "Hey, we just saw something weird". Underwood then went up and filmed it, and von Renenamp also mentions radar hits. If the video is what they say, it is a recording of the same object the pilots saw with their own eyes.
